title: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus), Chapter 23
language: Greek (Codex Sinaiticus) / English (King James Version Apocrypha)
source: Codex Sinaiticus folio + transcription (codexsinaiticus.org) + King James Version Apocrypha (1611; 1769 text)
description: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) chapter 23. Manuscript page scan(s) from Codex Sinaiticus hosted by the Codex Sinaiticus Project, with the Project's verbatim transcription of the Greek and the English of King James Version Apocrypha (1611; 1769 text).
introduction:
This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: The actual folio(s) of Codex Sinaiticus containing this chapter, from the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). Each section links to the specific folio holding its verses.
  2. Original text: The Codex Sinaiticus Project's verbatim transcription of the folio shown (uncial letters, lunate sigma, nomina sacra preserved).
  3. English translation: King James Version Apocrypha (1611; 1769 text), public domain, retrieved verbatim from ebible.org eng-kjv USFM (KJV with Apocrypha).

Numbering: Verse numbering of Sirach differs between the Greek manuscripts, Rahlfs, and the KJV in many chapters. Compare by content rather than by number.

Numbering: English verse 28 has no Greek under that number in the codex as transcribed. Compare by content.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>κε περ · και δεϲποτα ζωηϲ μου ˙ μη εγκαταλιπηϲ με · εν βουλη αυτω · μη αφηϲ με · πεϲιν εν αυτοιϲ · <sup>2</sup>τιϲ επιϲτηϲει · επι του διανοηματοϲ μου · μαϲτιγαϲ · και επι τηϲ καρδιαϲ · μου · παιδει αν ϲοφιαϲ · ϊνα επι τοιϲ αγνοημαϲιν μου · μη φειϲωνται · και ου μη παρη · τα αμαρτηματα αυτω · <sup>3</sup>οπωϲ μη πληθυνθωϲιν · αι αγνοιαι μου · και αι αμαρτιαι μου · πλεοναϲωϲιν ˙ και πεϲουμαι · εναντι των ϋπεναντιων ˙ και επιχαρειται μοι · ο εχθροϲ μου ˙ <sup>4</sup>κε περ · και θεε ζωηϲ μου ˙ μετεωριϲμον οφθαλμων . μη δωϲ μοι ˙ <sup>5</sup>και επιθυμιαν · αποϲτρεψον απ εμου ˙ <sup>6</sup>κοιλιαϲ ορεξιϲ · και ϲυνουϲιαϲμοϲ · μη καταλαβετωϲαν με · και ψυχη αναιδει · μη παραδωϲ με · <sup>7</sup>παιδιαν ϲτοματοϲ · ακουϲατε τεκνα ˙ και ο φυλαϲϲων · ου μη αλω · <sup>8</sup>εν τοιϲ χειλεϲιν αυτου · καταλειφθηϲεται αμαρτωλοϲ · και λοιδοριαι και ϋπερηφανοϲ · ϲκανδαλιϲθηϲονται εν αυτοιϲ ·
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>O Lord, Father and Governor of all my whole life, leave me not to their counsels, and let me not fall by them. <sup>2</sup>Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over mine heart? that they spare me not for mine ignorances, and it pass not by my sins: <sup>3</sup>Lest mine ignorances increase, and my sins abound to my destruction, and I fall before mine adversaries, and mine enemy rejoice over me, whose hope is far from thy mercy. <sup>4</sup>O Lord, Father and God of my life, give me not a proud look, but turn away from thy servants always a haughty mind. <sup>5</sup>Turn away from me vain hopes and concupiscence, and thou shalt hold him up that is desirous always to serve thee. <sup>6</sup>Let not the greediness of the belly nor lust of the flesh take hold of me; and give not over me thy servant into an impudent mind. <sup>7</sup>Hear, O ye children, the discipline of the mouth: he that keepeth it shall never be taken in his lips. <sup>8</sup>The sinner shall be left in his foolishness: both the evil speaker and the proud shall fall thereby.

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>ορκω . μη εθειϲηϲ το ϲτομα ϲου ˙ και ονομαϲια του αγιου · μη ϲυνεθιϲθηϲ <sup>10</sup>ωϲπερ γαρ οικετηϲ · εξεταζομενοϲ ενδελεχωϲ · απο μωλωποϲ · ουκ ελαττωθηϲεται · ουτωϲ και ο ομνυων · και ο ονομαζων δια παντοϲ απο αμαρτιαϲ · ου μη καθαριϲθη ˙ <sup>11</sup>ανηρ πολυορκοϲ · πληϲθηϲεται ανομιαϲ · και ουκ αποϲτηϲεται απο του οικου αυτου · μαϲτιγξ εαν πλημμεληϲη · αμαρτια αυτου επ αυτω · και εαν ϋπερϊδη · ημαρτεν διϲϲωϲ ˙ και ει δια καινηϲ ωμοϲεν . ου δικαιωθηϲεται ˙ πληϲθηϲεται ˙ γαρ επαγωγων . ο οικοϲ αυτου · <sup>12</sup>εϲτιν λεξιϲ · αντιπεριβεβλημενη θανατω · μη ευρεθητω . εν κληρονομια ϊακωβʼ απο γαρ ευϲεβων · ταυτα παντα αποϲτηϲεται ˙ και εν αμαρτιαιϲ · ουκ ενκυλιϲθηϲονται · <sup>13</sup>απαιδευϲιαν αϲυρη · μη εθιϲηϲ το ϲτομα ϲου · εϲτιν γαρ εν αυτη · λογοϲ αμαρτιαϲ · <sup>14</sup>μνηϲθητι πρϲ ϲου · και μρϲ ϲου · ανα μεϲον γαρ μεγιϲτανων . ϲυνεδρευϲειϲ · μηποτε επιλαθη . ενωπιον αυτων · και τω εθιϲμω ϲου μωρανθηϲ · και θεληϲειϲ · ει μη εγεννηθηϲ · και την ημεραν του τοκετου ϲου · καταραϲη <sup>15</sup>ανοϲ ϲυνεθιζομενοϲ λογοιϲ ονιδιϲμου · εν παϲαιϲ ταιϲ ημεραιϲ αυτου · ου μη παιδευθη · <sup>16</sup>δυο ειδη · πληθυνουϲιν αμαρτιαϲ · και το τριτον . επαξει οργην ·
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>Accustom not thy mouth to swearing; neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One. <sup>10</sup>For as a servant that is continually beaten shall not be without a blue mark: so he that sweareth and nameth God continually shall not be faultless. <sup>11</sup>A man that useth much swearing shall be filled with iniquity, and the plague shall never depart from his house: if he shall offend, his sin shall be upon him: and if he acknowledge not his sin, he maketh a double offence: and if he swear in vain, he shall not be innocent, but his house shall be full of calamities. <sup>12</sup>There is a word that is clothed about with death: God grant that it be not found in the heritage of Jacob; for all such things shall be far from the godly, and they shall not wallow in their sins. <sup>13</sup>Use not thy mouth to intemperate swearing, for therein is the word of sin. <sup>14</sup>Remember thy father and thy mother, when thou sittest among great men. Be not forgetful before them, and so thou by thy custom become a fool, and wish that thou hadst not been born, and curse they day of thy nativity. <sup>15</sup>The man that is accustomed to opprobrious words will never be reformed all the days of his life. <sup>16</sup>Two sorts of men multiply sin, and the third will bring wrath: a hot mind is as a burning fire, it will never be quenched till it be consumed: a fornicator in the body of his flesh will never cease till he hath kindled a fire.

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>ψυχη θερμη . ωϲ πυρ καιομενον ˙ ου μη ϲβεϲθη . εωϲ αν καταποθη · ανοϲ πορνοϲ · εν ϲωματι ϲαρκοϲ αυτου · ου μη παυϲηται . εωϲ αν εκκαυϲη πυρ · ανω πορνω . παϲ αρτοϲ ηδυϲ ˙ ου μη κοπαϲη . εωϲ αν τελευτηϲη · <sup>18</sup>ανοϲ παραβαινων απο τηϲ κλινηϲ αυτου · λεγων εν ψυχη αυτου · τιϲ με ορα ˙ ϲκοτοϲ κυκλω μου · και τοιχοι με καλυπτουϲιν · και ουθειϲ με ορα · τι ευλαβουμαι ˙ των αμαρτιων μου · ου μη μνηϲθηϲεται ο ψιϲτοϲ ˙ <sup>19</sup>και οφθαλμοι ανων . ο φοβοϲ αυτου ˙ και ουκ εγνω · οτι οφθαλμοι κυ . μυριοπλαϲιωϲ ηλιου φωτινοτεροι ˙ επιβλεποντεϲ · παϲαϲ οδουϲ ανων ˙ και κατανοουντεϲ · ειϲ αποκρυφα μερη · <sup>20</sup>πριν η κτιϲθηναι . τα παντα εγνωϲται αυτω ουτωϲ και μετα το ϲυντελεϲθηναι · <sup>21</sup>ουτοϲ εν πλατιαιϲ πολεωϲ · εκδικηθηϲεται ˙ και ου ουχ ϋπενοηϲεν · πιαϲθηϲεται ˙ <sup>22</sup>ουτωϲ και γυνη καταλιπουϲα τον ανδρα · και παριϲτωϲα κληρονομον · εξ αλλοτριου <sup>23</sup>πρωτον μεν γαρ . εν νομω ϋψιϲτου ηπιθηϲεν · και δευτερον . ειϲ ανδρα αυτηϲ επλημμεληϲεν · και το τριτον . εν πορνια εμοιχευθη ˙ και εξ αλλοτριου ανδροϲ · τεκνα παρεϲτηϲεν <sup>24</sup>αυτη · ειϲ εκκληϲιαν εξαχθηϲεται ˙ και επι τα τεκνα αυτηϲ · επιϲκοπη εϲται ˙
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>All bread is sweet to a whoremonger, he will not leave off till he die. <sup>18</sup>A man that breaketh wedlock, saying thus in his heart, Who seeth me? I am compassed about with darkness, the walls cover me, and no body seeth me; what need I to fear? the most High will not remember my sins: <sup>19</sup>Such a man only feareth the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts. <sup>20</sup>He knew all things ere ever they were created; so also after they were perfected he looked upon them all. <sup>21</sup>This man shall be punished in the streets of the city, and where he suspecteth not he shall be taken. <sup>22</sup>Thus shall it go also with the wife that leaveth her husband, and bringeth in an heir by another. <sup>23</sup>For first, she hath disobeyed the law of the most High; and secondly, she hath trespassed against her own husband; and thirdly, she hath played the whore in adultery, and brought children by another man. <sup>24</sup>She shall be brought out into the congregation, and inquisition shall be made of her children.

translation.original_text: <sup>25</sup>ου διαδωϲουϲιν τα τεκνα αυτηϲ · ειϲ ριζαν · και οι κλαδοι αυτηϲ · ουκ οιϲουϲιν καρπον · <sup>26</sup>καταλιψει ειϲ καταραν . το μνημοϲυνον αυτηϲ · και το ονειδοϲ αυτηϲ · ουκ εξαλιφθηϲεται <sup>27</sup>και επιγνωϲονται οι καταλειφθεντεϲ · οτι ουθεν κριττον . φοβου κυ ˙ και ουθεν γλυκυτερον · του προϲεχειν εντολαιϲ κυ · ϲοφιαϲ αινεϲιϲ
translation.text: <sup>25</sup>Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit. <sup>26</sup>She shall leave her memory to be cursed, and her reproach shall not be blotted out. <sup>27</sup>And they that remain shall know that there is nothing better than the fear of the Lord, and that there is nothing sweeter than to take heed unto the commandments of the Lord. <sup>28</sup>It is great glory to follow the Lord, and to be received of him is long life.
